alternatives: Lacosamide is a non-enzyme-inducing alternative if levetiracetam worsens mood or anxiety
contraindications: Enzyme-inducing antiseizure drugs (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital) increase dexamethasone clearance and interact with chemotherapy and sertraline; avoid when a non-inducing agent is suitable.
interactions: Dexamethasone and sertraline: SSRIs with systemic corticosteroids increase upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk; consider gastric protection.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right frontal 3.8 cm lesion involving the precentral and middle frontal gyri with thick irregular incomplete ring enhancement and a medial enhancing nodule, central FLAIR hypointensity, no central restricted diffusion and only minimal rim restriction, extensive edema and 3 mm midline shift, plus a separate 8 mm non-enhancing ovoid left frontal white matter lesion
action_criteria.label: Order MRI brain with and without gadolinium contrast (tumor protocol with DWI, FLAIR, post-contrast T1) to characterize the right frontal lobe lesion, define mass effect, and plan surgery
action_criteria.rationale: Contrast MRI characterizes the lesion and its mimics, defines the mass effect and its relation to motor cortex, and plans the approach (EANO 2021).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: rCBV 4.2 at the enhancing rim supports a high-grade neoplasm over tumefactive demyelination and targets the sampling
action_criteria.label: Order MR perfusion imaging (DSC perfusion) to assess tumor vascularity and target highest-grade region for biopsy
action_criteria.rationale: Perfusion supports a high-grade neoplasm (rCBV above 1.75); tumefactive demyelination and tuberculoma usually have low rCBV. Tissue decides the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Cho/NAA 5.2 with lipid-lactate at the rim and raised choline beyond the enhancing margin support an infiltrative high-grade neoplasm
action_criteria.label: Order MR spectroscopy (1H-MRS) to characterize tumor metabolic profile
action_criteria.rationale: Choline elevation beyond enhancement supports infiltrative glioma; a tuberculoma usually shows a lipid peak without marked choline rise.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Right frontocentral focal delta slowing and mild generalized slowing, two equivocal contralateral left temporal sharp transients, no definite epileptiform discharges or seizures
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG to characterize the 10-second staring spell with amnesia
action_criteria.rationale: A single witnessed 10-second staring spell with amnesia may be a focal impaired-awareness seizure; the EEG characterizes it, and levetiracetam is started only if the spells are judged to be seizures (AIOM).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No extracranial primary malignancy identified, supporting primary brain tumor as the working diagnosis
action_criteria.label: Order CT chest/abdomen/pelvis as staging to exclude an extracranial primary if a solitary metastasis is on the differential

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal blood count, electrolytes and coagulation with a negative beta-hCG; ESR 28 mm/hr and CRP 8.2 mg/L only mildly raised without leukocytosis: no contraindication to surgery

action_criteria.rationale: Platelets, coagulation, electrolytes and type and screen must be known before a neurosurgical procedure and before dexamethasone.

action_criteria.rationale: The lesion involves the precentral gyrus; functional MRI plans the extent of a maximal safe resection (EANO 2021).

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture: the 3 mm midline shift, frontal horn effacement and right disc blurring carry a herniation risk
Do not initiate definitive tumor-directed therapy (radiation, temozolomide, alkylating chemotherapy) before tissue diagnosis is established
Do not start therapeutic anticoagulation without a clear thromboembolic indication, given upcoming neurosurgical intervention and bleeding risk
Do not treat the lesion as tumefactive demyelination (high-dose methylprednisolone or plasma exchange) or as a tuberculoma (empirical antituberculous therapy) without tissue
required_recommendations: Refer urgently to neurosurgery for maximal safe resection of the right frontal lesion, with preoperative functional MRI and DTI tractography and intraoperative mapping, with stereotactic biopsy if resection is not safely feasible; send the specimen for an integrated histomolecular diagnosis (WHO CNS5).
Characterise the 10-second staring spell with amnesia with an EEG; start levetiracetam only if it is judged to be a seizure, not as prophylaxis.

Start dexamethasone for symptomatic vasogenic oedema (for example 4 mg every 6 to 8 hours after a loading dose when mass effect is marked) at the lowest effective dose, with glucose monitoring and gastric protection, and taper after surgery.
Before temozolomide, arrange effective contraception (temozolomide is teratogenic).

After the integrated diagnosis, refer to the neuro-oncology multidisciplinary team; for glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, at age 70 or under with KPS 70 or more, radiotherapy 60 Gy in 30 fractions with concomitant and adjuvant temozolomide (Stupp 2005; EANO 2021).

patient.history_present_illness: This 44-year-old right-handed woman presents to the neurology service after referral from her primary care physician for evaluation of progressive headaches and behavioral changes over the past two months. The patient has a long-standing history of migraine without aura, typically experiencing 1-2 episodic throbbing headaches per month that respond well to sumatriptan and acetaminophen. Approximately eight weeks ago, the character of her headaches changed: they became more persistent, bilateral, with a pressure-like quality different from her usual migraines, and are notably worse in the morning upon awakening. On several occasions the headaches have woken her from sleep. Sumatriptan no longer provides relief, and over-the-counter analgesics are only partially effective. She initially attributed these symptoms to a recurrence of her chronic sinusitis, which had flared six weeks ago and was treated with a course of azithromycin. Despite completion of antibiotics, the headaches persisted and have progressively worsened. Over the past three weeks, her husband has noticed behavioral changes that he describes as out of character: she has become more irritable, occasionally short-tempered with her students at the high school where she teaches biology, and has twice forgotten to prepare lesson plans she had promised. She misplaced her car keys on three occasions and once could not recall the name of a colleague she has worked with for over a decade. These episodes have caused her significant distress, which she attributes to worsening anxiety. She also describes a vague, intermittent tingling sensation in her left hand and occasional clumsiness when writing on the whiteboard, which she has noticed over the past two to three weeks. Her husband witnessed one episode where she appeared to briefly stare blankly for about 10 seconds while cooking, after which she resumed her activity as if nothing had happened; she has no recollection of this event. She denies frank weakness, visual changes, difficulty swallowing, or gait instability. She denies fever, chills, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss. Of note, she has a remote history of pulmonary tuberculosis treated at age 22 in Guatemala. Her younger sister has multiple sclerosis, diagnosed five years ago. A non-contrast head CT ordered by her primary care physician showed a right frontal hypodense lesion with surrounding edema and 3 mm leftward midline shift, prompting urgent neurology consultation and inpatient admission for further workup.

neurological_exam.additional: Patient reports that her headaches have changed in character over the past two months — they are no longer episodic and responsive to sumatriptan but have become persistent and worse in the morning, sometimes waking her from sleep. Husband reports subtle behavioral changes over three weeks: increased irritability, uncharacteristic forgetfulness, and one episode where she seemed to 'zone out' for approximately 10 seconds while cooking, which they attributed to her anxiety.
